commissions.name: Bienal de São Paulo
commissions.summary: One of the oldest and largest biennials in the world, held in Oscar Niemeyer's Ciccillo Matarazzo Pavilion in Ibirapuera Park. Each edition's curatorial team selects participants and the foundation produces a substantial share of the works shown, including newly commissioned pieces.
commissions.budgetNote: Production budgets, travel and artist fees are negotiated case by case with the foundation's production team and are not published; confirm terms directly.
commissions.cycleNote: Biennial, historically in even-numbered years, with the curatorial team and artist list announced roughly a year ahead. No open call for artists.

commissions.name: Bienal do Mercosul
commissions.org: Fundação Bienal de Artes Visuais do Mercosul
commissions.summary: Large-scale biennial in Rio Grande do Sul with a strong pedagogical programme, showing artists from across the Southern Cone and beyond and producing new work for each edition.
commissions.budgetNote: Production support is arranged per project through the foundation; amounts are not publicly listed.
commissions.cycleNote: Roughly biennial, though the calendar has slipped between editions. Artists are curator-selected rather than chosen by open call.

commissions.name: Bienal de La Habana
commissions.org: Centro de Arte Contemporáneo Wifredo Lam / Ministerio de Cultura de Cuba
commissions.summary: Founded in 1984 as a biennial centred on artists from the Global South, staged across museums, Old Havana streets and sites such as the Morro-Cabaña fortress. Works are frequently produced on site with the organisers' support.
commissions.budgetNote: Material and production assistance is negotiated with the organisers; artists have often had to cover or co-fund travel. Confirm current arrangements.
commissions.cycleNote: Nominally every two to three years, but the calendar has been repeatedly disrupted; check the Centro Wifredo Lam for the status of the next edition.

commissions.name: Bienal de Arte Paiz
commissions.org: Fundación Paiz para la Educación y la Cultura
commissions.summary: Central America's longest-running visual arts biennial, using historic buildings in Guatemala City's Centro Histórico. Recent editions have combined a curator-invited core with an open call and an accompanying education and mediation programme.
commissions.budgetNote: Selected projects receive production support from the foundation; amounts vary by edition and are not published in advance.
commissions.cycleNote: Biennial. Open-call announcements are made by the Fundación Paiz several months before each edition.

commissions.name: Bienal de Cuenca
commissions.summary: Municipally backed biennial in Cuenca's UNESCO-listed historic centre, with a curatorial selection and, in several editions, an open call or regional nomination component.
commissions.budgetNote: Production and shipping support is handled by the municipal foundation on a per-project basis; verify what is covered for your edition.
commissions.cycleNote: Biennial in principle, with some editions delayed. Calls, when issued, are published by the Fundación Municipal.

commissions.name: Kingston Biennial
commissions.summary: The National Gallery of Jamaica's flagship exhibition, relaunched in 2022 as the Kingston Biennial with a curated format replacing the older submission-based National Biennial. New commissions by Jamaican and diaspora artists feature prominently.
commissions.budgetNote: Commission and production support comes through the gallery's exhibition budget; not publicly itemised.
commissions.cycleNote: Biennial in intent since the 2022 relaunch. Participation is by curatorial invitation; the gallery no longer runs the old juried submission route.

commissions.name: Ghetto Biennale
commissions.summary: Artist-organised biennial in the Grand Rue district, where visiting artists collaborate with the Atis Rezistans sculptors' collective to make work in situ. Explicitly framed as an experiment in who gets to travel and exhibit.
commissions.budgetNote: Historically not a funded commission: participants raise their own travel and material costs, with local collaboration and workspace provided. Confirm current terms with the organisers.
commissions.cycleNote: Roughly biennial via an open call, but editions have been postponed or restructured in response to the security situation in Port-au-Prince.

commissions.name: Premio Luis Caballero
commissions.summary: Bogotá's award for mid-career and senior artists, which funds and stages a major solo project in a city venue rather than simply granting a cash prize. Named after the painter Luis Caballero.
commissions.budgetNote: Winners receive a production budget plus prize money through IDARTES; amounts are set per edition in the published bases del concurso.
commissions.cycleNote: Held periodically (historically every two years) as part of IDARTES' calls; check the current Programa Distrital de Estímulos portfolio for the open period.

commissions.name: Programa Distrital de Estímulos
commissions.org: Instituto Distrital de las Artes (IDARTES), Secretaría de Cultura de Bogotá
commissions.summary: Bogotá's annual portfolio of grants, prizes and residencies across visual arts, public art, performance and music, open to artists and collectives based in or working with the city.
commissions.budgetNote: Each line carries its own published award value; consult the annual cartilla for current figures.
commissions.cycleNote: Annual cycle, with the full catalogue of calls published early in the year and individual lines closing on staggered dates.

commissions.name: Programa Nacional de Estímulos
commissions.org: Ministerio de las Culturas, las Artes y los Saberes
commissions.summary: Colombia's national grants and residencies programme, covering creation, research, circulation and international residency placements for Colombian artists and cultural workers.
commissions.budgetNote: Award values are fixed per line in the annual convocatoria document.
commissions.cycleNote: Annual, with the consolidated call published by the ministry and individual lines closing throughout the year.

commissions.name: Fondart (Fondo Nacional de Desarrollo Cultural y las Artes)
commissions.org: Ministerio de las Culturas, las Artes y el Patrimonio
commissions.summary: Chile's principal public arts fund, with national and regional windows supporting creation, production, research and circulation across visual arts, media arts and other disciplines.
commissions.budgetNote: Ceilings differ by line and region and are restated each year in the bases de concurso.
commissions.cycleNote: Annual competitive round administered through the Fondos de Cultura platform; applicants generally must be Chilean nationals or legal residents.

commissions.name: MetroArte
commissions.summary: Long-running programme placing large-scale artworks — murals, reliefs, sculptural interventions — in Santiago metro stations, including works by artists such as Roberto Matta and Mario Toral.
commissions.budgetNote: Works are typically realised through sponsorship, donation or partnership arrangements rather than a standing published commission budget.
commissions.cycleNote: No open call. Projects arise with station construction and renovation, negotiated directly with Metro de Santiago and partner sponsors.

commissions.name: Sistema de Apoyos a la Creación y Proyectos Culturales (formerly FONCA)
commissions.summary: Mexico's federal support system for creators, successor to FONCA, including fellowships for young creators, established creators and project-based production grants.
commissions.budgetNote: Monthly stipends and project amounts are set per programme line in each year's convocatoria; the structure has changed since the FONCA reorganisation, so verify current lines.
commissions.cycleNote: Annual calls published by the Secretaría de Cultura, generally restricted to Mexican nationals or residents.

commissions.name: Rumos Itaú Cultural
commissions.summary: Itaú Cultural's national programme selecting projects from across Brazil for production support, mentorship and circulation, spanning visual arts, performance, literature and hybrid practices.
commissions.budgetNote: Selected projects receive a production grant plus mentoring; the amount is fixed per edition in the edital.
commissions.cycleNote: Runs in editions rather than strictly annually; watch Itaú Cultural's editais page for the next open period.

commissions.name: ProAC Editais
commissions.org: Secretaria da Cultura, Economia e Indústria Criativas do Estado de São Paulo
commissions.summary: São Paulo state's programme of public calls funding production and circulation across visual arts, theatre, dance, music, film and cultural heritage projects.
commissions.budgetNote: Each edital sets its own award value and number of prizes; consult the current year's published list.
commissions.cycleNote: Rolling series of editais released through the year by the state culture secretariat, generally requiring proponents domiciled in São Paulo state.

commissions.name: Becas y Subsidios del Fondo Nacional de las Artes
commissions.summary: Argentina's national arts fund, offering creation grants, subsidies and prizes to individual artists and cultural organisations across disciplines.
commissions.budgetNote: Grant amounts are published per line and have varied considerably with inflation; check the current convocatoria.
commissions.cycleNote: Annual and periodic calls announced on the FNA site; open to Argentine nationals and residents.

commissions.name: Estímulos Económicos para la Cultura
commissions.summary: Peru's national competitive funding scheme, with lines for visual arts, cinema, performing arts, publishing and safeguarding of traditional cultural expressions.
commissions.budgetNote: Award amounts are defined per line in the annual bases; confirm current figures with the ministry.
commissions.cycleNote: Annual round with staggered closing dates by line, administered online by the Ministerio de Cultura.

commissions.name: Bienal de Artes Mediales de Santiago
commissions.org: Corporación Chilena de Video y Artes Electrónicas
commissions.summary: Chile's long-running media arts biennial, covering video, electronic and computational art, sound and installation, with exhibitions across Santiago venues.
commissions.budgetNote: Production support for selected works is arranged per edition and typically modest; confirm with the organisers.
commissions.cycleNote: Biennial, with open calls for specific sections published alongside curator-invited projects.

commissions.name: FILE — Festival Internacional de Linguagem Eletrônica
commissions.summary: Annual electronic language festival in São Paulo showing interactive installations, games, machinima, generative and net art from Brazilian and international practitioners.
commissions.budgetNote: Selection is primarily for exhibition; artist fees and production or shipping support are limited and negotiated individually. Confirm before budgeting.
commissions.cycleNote: Annual open call for submissions, published on the FILE site ahead of each edition.

commissions.name: Festival Internacional de la Imagen
commissions.summary: University-run festival and conference on digital and media art, design and creative technology, combining exhibitions, performances and an academic programme.
commissions.budgetNote: Primarily an exhibition and presentation platform; financial support for selected work is limited and should be confirmed with the organisers.
commissions.cycleNote: Annual, with an open call for works and papers issued by the Universidad de Caldas.

commissions.name: CIFO Grants and Commissions Program
commissions.summary: Founded by Ella Fontanals-Cisneros, this programme awards grants and commissions to Latin American and Latin American–born artists, with the resulting works shown in a group exhibition. Based outside the region but one of its most significant dedicated commissioning routes; the foundation has also operated CIFO Europa in Madrid.
commissions.budgetNote: Historically split into emerging-artist grants and larger mid-career commissions with defined award values; the structure has changed over time, so verify the current terms and geography before applying.
commissions.cycleNote: Periodic open call rather than a guaranteed annual round; confirm whether a cycle is currently running.

commissions.name: SUD – Salon Urbain de Douala
commissions.summary: Triennial urban art event run by the art centre doual'art, which commissions permanent and temporary artworks sited in Douala's neighbourhoods and developed with residents. doual'art was founded in 1991 by Marilyn Douala Manga Bell and the late Didier Schaub.
commissions.budgetNote: Production budgets are agreed project by project and typically cover fabrication and installation rather than a set artist fee; confirm current terms with doual'art.
commissions.cycleNote: Broadly triennial, with artists chosen through a mix of curatorial invitation and calls; the interval between editions has shifted, so confirm the live calendar.

commissions.name: Dak'Art — Biennale de l'Art Africain Contemporain
commissions.org: Secrétariat général de la Biennale de Dakar
commissions.summary: Africa's longest-running contemporary art biennale. Its main International Exhibition is selected by jury from an open call to artists from Africa and the African diaspora, alongside an invited curatorial programme and an off-programme (Dak'Art Off).
commissions.budgetNote: Selected artists generally receive production, shipping and hosting support rather than an artist fee; confirm what the current edition covers.
commissions.cycleNote: Nominally biennial, but recent editions have been postponed and rescheduled — verify the current edition's dates with the Secrétariat général before planning.

commissions.name: Rencontres de Bamako — Biennale Africaine de la Photographie
commissions.org: Ministère de la Culture du Mali with Institut français
commissions.summary: Pan-African photography biennale presenting a curated Exposition panafricaine drawn largely from an open call, plus invited exhibitions across venues in Bamako.
commissions.budgetNote: Selected photographers are normally supported with printing, framing and travel rather than a fee; confirm the current edition's terms.
commissions.cycleNote: Biennial in principle; several recent editions have been delayed or disrupted, so confirm whether a call is currently open.

commissions.name: Lagos Biennial
commissions.summary: Artist-founded biennial initiated in 2017 by Folakunle Oshun, staging large-scale commissions and installations in non-traditional Lagos venues, with participants drawn from both open call and curatorial invitation.
commissions.budgetNote: Production support is offered for selected commissions; scale varies considerably by edition and by project.
commissions.cycleNote: Irregular rather than strictly biennial — editions have not followed a fixed two-year rhythm. Watch the biennial's channels for the next call.

commissions.name: ART X Prize with Access
commissions.summary: Prize for an emerging Nigeria-based artist that funds and presents a newly commissioned work at the ART X Lagos art fair, with mentorship from an established artist.
commissions.budgetNote: Cash prize plus production support for the commissioned work; confirm the current amount, which has changed between editions.
commissions.cycleNote: Annual open call, generally launched several months ahead of the fair. Treat any specific closing date as unconfirmed.

commissions.name: New Dimensions
commissions.summary: Commissioning and mentorship programme for African artists making immersive and interactive work — VR/AR, 360 film, interactive documentary — combining a creative lab with production funding.
commissions.budgetNote: Production funding plus lab participation and mentorship; amounts vary by cycle and are best confirmed against the live call.
commissions.cycleNote: Calls run periodically as funding allows rather than on a fixed annual date.

commissions.name: Norval Sovereign African Art Prize
commissions.org: Norval Foundation with The Sovereign Art Foundation
commissions.summary: Pan-African art prize in which artists are put forward by a panel of nominators rather than applying directly; a shortlist is exhibited at Norval Foundation in Cape Town.
commissions.budgetNote: Cash awards to the winner and finalists, with a portion of proceeds directed to charitable programmes; confirm current prize values.
commissions.cycleNote: Runs in editions rather than on a guaranteed annual schedule — confirm whether a round is currently open.

commissions.name: Kampala Art Biennale
commissions.summary: Biennial of contemporary African art founded in 2014 by Daudi Karungi, combining invited artists with open participation and, in some editions, a master-class model pairing established and emerging artists.
commissions.budgetNote: Support is typically production and hosting rather than a fee; confirm per edition.
commissions.cycleNote: Biennial since 2014, though edition timing has moved; check for the current call.

commissions.name: Rainmaker Art Initiative
commissions.summary: Artist development and commissioning strand attached to MOWAA's campus in Benin City, offering production support, studio time and presentation opportunities to artists working in and with Nigeria.
commissions.budgetNote: Support reported to include production costs and studio access; amounts and inclusions are not publicly fixed — confirm with MOWAA.
commissions.cycleNote: Runs in cohorts announced by MOWAA rather than on a fixed calendar.

commissions.name: Biennale de Lubumbashi (Rencontres Picha)
commissions.summary: Artist-led biennial founded in 2008 by a group including Sammy Baloji, presenting commissions, screenings and public interventions across sites in Lubumbashi.
commissions.budgetNote: Project-based production support; confirm terms directly with Picha.
commissions.cycleNote: Biennial in intent, with variable intervals between editions.

commissions.name: Fak'ugesi African Digital Innovation Festival
commissions.org: Tshimologong Digital Innovation Precinct, University of the Witwatersrand
commissions.summary: Festival and platform in Braamfontein pairing African digital artists with technologists, historically including residencies, commissions and showcases of digital and interactive work.
commissions.budgetNote: Residency and commission support has varied year to year; confirm what is currently funded.
commissions.cycleNote: Historically annual around the second half of the year; confirm that the festival is running in the current cycle before relying on it.

commissions.name: Chale Wote Street Art Festival
commissions.summary: Street art and performance festival in the Jamestown/Ga Mashie district of Accra, programming murals, installations, performance and film in public space through an open call to artists.
commissions.budgetNote: Production support is limited and many participants cover their own costs; confirm what, if anything, is provided.
commissions.cycleNote: Annual, historically around August, with the open call issued some months ahead.

commissions.name: Africa No Filter grants
commissions.summary: Grant-maker supporting storytellers, artists and cultural organisations working to shift narratives about Africa, funding projects across visual art, media and cultural production on the continent.
commissions.budgetNote: Grant sizes vary by programme strand; confirm current ceilings and eligible costs against the live call.
commissions.cycleNote: Rolling and cyclical calls across several strands rather than one fixed annual deadline.

commissions.name: Art in Transit
commissions.summary: A long-running civic scheme, begun with the North East Line in the early 2000s and continued through the Circle, Downtown and Thomson-East Coast lines, that integrates commissioned artworks into Singapore's MRT stations. Works are developed alongside station architecture rather than applied afterwards, and commissions are tied to the build-out of new rail lines, so opportunities appear in waves as lines are planned and constructed. Routes in have combined curatorial/panel selection with calls attached to specific lines. NOT RE-VERIFIED THIS SESSION: outbound web access was blocked by egress policy, so current status and the current selection route were not confirmed against LTA's own site.
commissions.budgetNote: Artwork budgets are drawn from station construction budgets rather than published as a standing figure. No current amount confirmed; treat any figure found elsewhere as unchecked and undated.
commissions.cycleNote: Not a fixed annual round. Selection runs in waves tied to new MRT line construction, mixing panel/curatorial selection with calls attached to specific lines. No dated deadline.

commissions.name: Bangkok Art Biennale
commissions.summary: A biennial founded in 2018 and staged across venues in Bangkok including temples (Wat Pho, Wat Arun, Wat Prayoon), riverside sites and central shopping-district and civic spaces, led by Apinan Poshyananda as chief executive and artistic director. The main exhibition commissions new work from artists chosen by the curatorial team and cannot generally be applied to directly, but editions have also run a separate early-career artist strand with its own entry route — which is why access is recorded here as mixed rather than invitation-only. NOT RE-VERIFIED THIS SESSION: web access was blocked, so the current edition, curatorial team and whether an early-career call is presently open were not confirmed.
commissions.budgetNote: Production support for commissioned works is negotiated per project with the organisers rather than published as a standing fee. No figure quoted because none could be confirmed or dated.
commissions.cycleNote: Biennial, with editions held in 2018, 2020, 2022 and 2024 and artist selection made by curators well in advance of each edition. Any early-career open call opens well ahead of the edition it feeds. No dated deadline.

commissions.name: Jakarta Biennale
commissions.summary: A periodic biennial in Jakarta, with roots in the Pameran Besar Seni Lukis Indonesia exhibitions of the 1970s and running under the Jakarta Biennale name since the 2000s, organised by Yayasan Jakarta Biennale. It commissions and presents new work, with a history of curatorial framings grounded in local social and urban conditions and in collective practice. Participation is by curatorial selection, not public application. NOT RE-VERIFIED THIS SESSION: web access was blocked, so current operating status was not confirmed. This biennial has had an irregular schedule with multi-year gaps between editions, so present activity in particular needs checking, as does the source domain below.
commissions.budgetNote: Commission and production support is arranged per project with the organising foundation. No published standing figure and no dated amount confirmed.
commissions.cycleNote: Nominally biennial but historically irregular, with editions announced ahead of each cycle rather than on a reliable calendar. No dated deadline.

commissions.name: Public Art Programme
commissions.summary: A council-run public art programme commissioning permanent and temporary work for civic sites, parks, town centres and transport and development projects across the Auckland region, guided by council public art policy and with stated commitments to Māori and Pacific artists in the public realm. Related commissioning also sits with council-controlled organisations and the council's urban development functions, so opportunities surface under more than one banner. Routes in have included expressions of interest for named projects alongside direct curatorial approaches. NOT RE-VERIFIED THIS SESSION: web access was blocked. The access mechanism in particular — whether an artist registry or EOI list is currently open — is unconfirmed and must be checked before publishing.
commissions.budgetNote: Individual commission budgets are set per project within council capital and development budgets rather than as a single published rate. No figure quoted because none could be confirmed or tied to a year.
commissions.cycleNote: Rolling rather than a single annual round, with opportunities tied to specific capital projects and precinct developments as they come forward. No dated deadline.

commissions.name: National Commission for Culture and the Arts grants
commissions.org: National Commission for Culture and the Arts (NCCA)
commissions.summary: The Philippine government's national arts and culture body, headquartered in Intramuros, Manila, which runs competitive grant rounds through its subcommissions and national committees, including those covering visual arts. Grants support the creation, presentation and documentation of new work, so this is a genuine application route rather than an invitation-only scheme. Eligibility is normally restricted to Filipino nationals and Philippine-registered organisations, and proposals are assessed by the relevant national committee. NOT RE-VERIFIED THIS SESSION: web access was blocked, so the current round structure and eligibility rules were not confirmed.
commissions.budgetNote: Award sizes vary by grant line and committee and are set per round. No amount quoted because none could be confirmed or attached to a specific year.
commissions.cycleNote: Grant rounds run on an annual cycle, with applications submitted ahead of the following programme year. No dated deadline — check the current round calendar directly.

commissions.name: Setouchi Triennale (Setouchi International Art Festival)
commissions.city: Takamatsu and the Seto Inland Sea islands (Naoshima, Teshima, Inujima, Shodoshima and others)
commissions.summary: Large-scale island-wide festival of site-specific commissions across the Seto Inland Sea, general-directed by Fram Kitagawa. Most works are new site-responsive commissions placed in disused houses, schools and harbours, developed with local island communities and often left in place between editions. Some editions add limited open-call strands for smaller community or performance projects alongside the invited artist list.
commissions.budgetNote: Production budgets are negotiated per project and are not published as a standard figure; travel, accommodation and local fabrication support are typically arranged by the executive committee. Confirm the current terms directly with the organisers.
commissions.cycleNote: Triennial, staged in spring, summer and autumn seasons across a single year (recent editions in 2019, 2022 and 2025). Artist selection happens well over a year in advance; there is no fixed public deadline, so track the official site for each edition's announcements.

commissions.name: Echigo-Tsumari Art Triennale (Echigo-Tsumari Art Field)
commissions.org: Echigo-Tsumari Art Triennale Executive Committee / NPO Echigo-Tsumari Satoyama Collaborative Organization
commissions.summary: Rural land-art field across roughly 760 square kilometres of terraced rice fields and depopulated villages, general-directed by Fram Kitagawa. Commissions are predominantly site-specific and community-embedded, with many works becoming permanent. Selection is mainly by invitation, but individual editions have run open calls for specific strands, and the Art Field operates year-round beyond the triennale itself.
commissions.budgetNote: Production support is agreed project by project rather than advertised as a fixed fee; materials, local labour and accommodation during installation are commonly covered. Treat any quoted figure as unconfirmed.
commissions.cycleNote: Roughly triennial, with recent editions in 2022 and 2024 after pandemic rescheduling, so the historic three-year rhythm has shifted. Check the official site for the next edition rather than assuming a fixed year.

commissions.name: Aichi Triennale
commissions.city: Nagoya and other sites in Aichi Prefecture
commissions.summary: Japan's largest prefecture-backed international art festival, spanning contemporary art, performing arts and film across the Aichi Arts Center and satellite venues in cities such as Seto and Tokoname. Each edition is shaped by an appointed artistic director who invites artists; a significant share of the visual-art programme is newly produced work rather than existing loans.
commissions.budgetNote: New-production budgets are set per commission by the organizing committee and are not published. Fees and production support should be confirmed during curatorial negotiation.
commissions.cycleNote: Triennial, with editions held in 2010, 2013, 2016, 2019, 2022 and 2025. There is no artist open call; curatorial research and invitation typically run one to two years ahead of the opening.

commissions.name: Yokohama Triennale
commissions.org: Organizing Committee for Yokohama Triennale (City of Yokohama, Japan Foundation, Yokohama Arts Foundation and partners)
commissions.summary: International contemporary art triennale centred on the Yokohama Museum of Art and additional harbour-front venues, with an artistic director or curatorial team appointed per edition. Includes newly commissioned works alongside loans, plus public-programme strands involving local organisations.
commissions.budgetNote: Commission and production budgets are handled internally per project and are not advertised. Confirm with the organizing committee.
commissions.cycleNote: Approximately triennial; the schedule has shifted since 2020 (editions in 2020 and 2024). Selection is curator-led with no artist open call.

commissions.name: Tokyo Artpoint Project
commissions.org: Arts Council Tokyo (Tokyo Metropolitan Foundation for History and Culture)
commissions.summary: Long-running civic art programme in which Arts Council Tokyo co-runs multi-year, community-embedded art projects with NPOs and local partners across Tokyo's wards and islands. Artists are usually engaged through the partner organisation delivering a given project rather than through a single central artist call, so entry is via the individual project teams.
commissions.budgetNote: Funding flows to the partner organisation under a co-production agreement rather than as a published per-artist commission fee; artist fees are set within each project's budget.
commissions.cycleNote: Rolling, multi-year projects. Arts Council Tokyo issues periodic calls for partner organisations rather than a fixed annual artist deadline; monitor the Arts Council Tokyo site for current openings.

commissions.name: MMCA Hyundai Motor Series
commissions.org: National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Korea (MMCA), supported by Hyundai Motor Company
commissions.summary: Annual single-artist commission at MMCA Seoul supporting a mid-career or established Korean artist to produce an ambitious new body of work for a dedicated large-scale exhibition. Established under a long-term corporate sponsorship agreement with Hyundai Motor and widely regarded as one of the most significant institutional commissions in Korea.
commissions.budgetNote: Substantial production support is provided through the sponsorship, but the per-artist budget is not publicly itemised; do not cite a specific figure without confirmation from MMCA.
commissions.cycleNote: One artist selected per year by the museum; selection is internal and by invitation, with no public application route.

commissions.name: Gwangju Biennale
commissions.summary: Asia's longest-running contemporary art biennale, founded in 1995 in the city associated with the May 1980 democratic uprising. Each edition is led by an appointed artistic director who invites artists, with a strong record of new production; separate strands such as the GB Commission have produced site-specific works in historically charged locations including the former Armed Forces Hospital.
commissions.budgetNote: Production budgets are negotiated per commission by the foundation and are not published. Confirm fee, fabrication and shipping terms in the artist agreement.
commissions.cycleNote: Biennial, with schedules occasionally shifted (a special edition marked the 30th anniversary of the biennale's founding city context). Curator-led invitation only; no artist open call.

commissions.name: Busan Biennale
commissions.summary: Biennial exhibition using the Busan Museum of Contemporary Art on Eulsukdo alongside port, harbour and heritage venues around the city, formed from the merger of earlier Busan sculpture and sea art events. Editions are directed by an appointed artistic director and regularly include newly produced site-responsive works.
commissions.budgetNote: New-work production is supported case by case; amounts are not published. Confirm with the organizing committee.
commissions.cycleNote: Biennial, opening in the second half of the year in even-numbered years. Selection is by curatorial invitation.

commissions.name: Seoul Mediacity Biennale
commissions.summary: Municipal biennale focused on media, moving image and technology-based practice, organised by the Seoul Museum of Art and staged mainly at its Seosomun main building with satellite venues. Editions regularly commission new moving-image and installation work and place emphasis on the social and political dimensions of media rather than technology showcases.
commissions.budgetNote: Commissioning budgets sit within the museum's biennale programme and are not published per artist; confirm terms with SeMA.
commissions.cycleNote: Biennial, directed by an appointed artistic director; artists are invited rather than selected through an open call.

commissions.name: ZER01NE Creators
commissions.summary: Corporate-funded creator platform based around the ZER01NE campus in Seoul, selecting a cohort of artists, designers and technologists each year to develop experimental projects, often in collaboration with Hyundai Motor Group engineers and partner startups. Oriented towards art-and-technology R&D and prototype production rather than exhibition-only commissions.
commissions.budgetNote: Selected creators receive project funding plus workspace and technical collaboration; amounts vary by project and year, so confirm the current package with ZER01NE before relying on any figure.
commissions.cycleNote: Annual open call for the creator cohort, typically announced in the first half of the year. Check the official site for the current round rather than assuming a fixed date.

commissions.name: Public Art Installation programme (1% for public art)
commissions.org: Ministry of Culture, Republic of China (Taiwan) — Public Art Office, with commissioning agencies
commissions.city: Nationwide (Taipei, Kaohsiung, Taichung, Tainan and other municipalities)
commissions.summary: Statutory public art system under Taiwan's Culture and the Arts Reward and Promotion Act, requiring public construction projects to allocate a share of their budget (commonly cited as not less than one percent) to public artworks. Individual projects are run by the commissioning agency through review committees, using open calls, limited invitation or shortlists drawn from artist registers, and all cases are published centrally on the Ministry of Culture's public art portal.
commissions.budgetNote: Budgets derive from a percentage of each construction project's cost, so they range from very small to multi-million-NTD commissions. The exact statutory percentage and thresholds have been amended over time — verify the current rule before publishing a figure.
commissions.cycleNote: Rolling. New cases appear continuously as public construction projects reach the art-allocation stage; the central portal is the practical place to monitor open calls and registration.

commissions.name: Taipei Biennial
commissions.summary: Taiwan's flagship international biennale, held at the Taipei Fine Arts Museum since 1998 in its international format, with curators appointed per edition. Editions typically include a substantial proportion of newly commissioned or newly produced work by Taiwanese and international artists.
commissions.budgetNote: Production support is arranged per commission by the museum and is not published. Confirm fee and fabrication terms with TFAM.
commissions.cycleNote: Biennial, usually opening in the late autumn of even-numbered years and running into the following year. Curator-led invitation only.

commissions.name: CREATORS and the Technology Media Platform
commissions.org: Taiwan Contemporary Culture Lab (C-LAB), Taiwan Living Arts Foundation
commissions.summary: Production and research programme on the former Air Force Command Headquarters site in central Taipei, supporting experimental art, sound, and technology-media projects. residencies.duration: Commonly three to twelve months depending on strand
residencies.funding: Studio provided, with production support and, for some strands, accommodation and a stipend; support differs between the two sites and between domestic and international strands
residencies.disciplines: Contemporary visual art, plus curators and researchers in some strands
residencies.summary: National residency programme of the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Korea, operating studio complexes at Changdong in northern Seoul and at Goyang. Combines long-stay studios for Korea-based artists with shorter international and exchange placements, and includes critique sessions, open studios and curatorial engagement with the museum.
residencies.applicationNote: Open call for the main strands, usually annual, alongside international exchange places arranged with partner institutions abroad. The programme has been restructured more than once, so confirm which studios and strands are currently running.

residencies.name: SeMA Nanji Residency
residencies.duration: Approximately one year for the main studio strand, with shorter international placements
residencies.funding: Studio provided with production support and programme costs covered; a living stipend is not guaranteed for all strands — confirm with the museum
residencies.disciplines: Contemporary visual art, plus critics and curators in dedicated strands
residencies.summary: Residency of the Seoul Museum of Art, located in the Nanjido area of the Sangam district on land reclaimed from a former landfill and now parkland. Focused on early- and mid-career Korea-based artists, with a structured programme of critiques, studio visits and open studios, plus a smaller international exchange strand.
residencies.applicationNote: Annual open call for the main artist and critic strands, generally announced in the autumn for the following year. International places are often arranged through exchange partnerships.

residencies.name: Incheon Art Platform
residencies.duration: Commonly three to twelve months depending on strand
residencies.funding: Studio and accommodation provided, with production support; stipend arrangements vary by strand and year — confirm with the foundation
residencies.disciplines: Contemporary visual art, performance, and curatorial and critical research
residencies.summary: Municipal arts complex in Incheon's Open Port area, converted from a cluster of early twentieth-century warehouses and commercial buildings, operated by the Incheon Foundation for Arts and Culture. Combines studios, exhibition halls and a performance space, with residents presenting open studios and exhibitions on site.
residencies.applicationNote: Annual open call with domestic and international strands. Selection is competitive and application material is often published in Korean first, with English versions on the international strand.

residencies.name: Gyeonggi Creation Center
residencies.duration: Commonly six months to a year
residencies.funding: Studio and accommodation provided with production support; confirm the current stipend and fee structure, which has changed with the centre's reorganisation
residencies.disciplines: Contemporary visual art, ecology- and community-oriented practice
residencies.summary: Residency on Daebudo, a coastal island area within Ansan, housed in a converted former marine research facility beside tidal flats. Its remote coastal setting has supported a strong strand of ecological and site-responsive work, and it has operated under the Gyeonggi provincial cultural bodies with its governance revised over the years.
residencies.applicationNote: Open call, generally annual, published mainly in Korean. Because the centre's operator and remit have been reorganised, verify the current programme and host body before applying.

residencies.name: Taipei Artist Village and Treasure Hill Artist Village
residencies.duration: Typically one to three months
residencies.funding: Studio and accommodation provided; a subsidy toward living or production costs is available in some strands, and travel is sometimes covered — confirm the current package
residencies.disciplines: Contemporary visual art, sound, performance, writing and interdisciplinary practice
residencies.summary: Twin residency sites operated by the Taipei Culture Foundation: the Taipei Artist Village near Shandao Temple in the city centre, and Treasure Hill Artist Village, a hillside settlement of former informal housing beside the Xindian River now repurposed as a village of studios and small galleries. Both host international and Taiwanese residents with regular open studios and exhibitions.
residencies.applicationNote: International open call, usually annual, alongside exchange placements with partner cities and organisations abroad. Applicants can normally indicate a site preference.

residencies.name: Kuandu Museum of Fine Arts Residency
residencies.duration: Commonly around two months
residencies.funding: Accommodation, studio, a stipend and travel support are typically offered, plus exhibition support; confirm current amounts with the museum
residencies.disciplines: Contemporary visual art
residencies.summary: Residency attached to the Kuandu Museum of Fine Arts on the campus of the Taipei National University of the Arts in the Guandu district of northern Taipei. Residents work in university-adjacent facilities with access to students and faculty, and the programme typically concludes with a presentation or exhibition at the museum.
residencies.applicationNote: International open call in most years, with a small cohort selected. Programme scale depends on annual museum funding, so confirm that a call is running for the current year.

residencies.name: Swatch Art Peace Hotel Artist Residency
residencies.duration: Commonly three to six months
residencies.funding: Accommodation and a combined living and studio space are provided free of charge by the corporate sponsor; a cash stipend is not the core of the offer, and materials support should be confirmed
residencies.disciplines: Visual art, music, writing, film and design
residencies.summary: Corporate-funded residency occupying upper floors of a restored historic building on the Bund in Shanghai, run by the Swatch Group. Provides combined live-work studios in a central location with a mixed international cohort across disciplines; artists are generally expected to leave a work with the collection or contribute to programming.
residencies.applicationNote: Applications are made directly to the residency, with selection by an internal jury; there is no fixed annual public deadline of record. Verify that the programme is currently accepting applications before listing it as live.

residencies.name: Institute for Provocation (IFP)
residencies.duration: Commonly one to three months
residencies.funding: Largely self-funded or externally funded: residents typically arrive with support from a home-country funder, with IFP providing studio space and local infrastructure
residencies.disciplines: Research-based art, architecture, design and curatorial practice
residencies.summary: Independent, research-oriented art and design organisation in Beijing running a residency alongside exhibitions, lectures and publishing. Emphasises discursive and research-driven practice and local collaboration rather than studio production for its own sake, and has historically worked with European partner funders to place residents.
residencies.applicationNote: Applications are handled directly and often in coordination with a funder in the artist's home country; there is no large standing open call. Independent spaces in Beijing operate under shifting conditions, so confirm current status before applying.

residencies.name: Red Gate Residency
residencies.duration: Commonly one to three months
residencies.funding: Fee-based: residents pay for studio and accommodation, and the programme is not funded through grants to artists
residencies.disciplines: Contemporary visual art across media
residencies.summary: Long-established fee-paying residency in Beijing founded by Brian Wallace of Red Gate Gallery, providing studio and apartment accommodation plus introductions to the local art scene, studio visits and gallery access. Historically one of the main routes for foreign artists to spend working time in Beijing.
residencies.applicationNote: Rolling applications for paid places rather than a competitive funded call. Operating patterns for foreign-artist residencies in Beijing changed considerably after 2020 — confirm the programme is currently running and check current fees before publishing.
